description: Use when the user wants a site's brand: its colors, fonts, logo, theme or social links - 'what colors does stripe use', 'match this brand', 'build something in the style of X'. Returns role colors (primary, accent, background, text) as hex with human-readable names, the wider palette, fonts by role, logo candidates, social profiles, dark/light theme, and a 0-1 confidence score with `signals` explaining where the colors came from: read signals.explanation and tell the user whether they were declared by the site ('css-var'/'theme-color') or inferred from usage frequency ('usage', a guess) - never present inferred colors as the official palette. Not for: markup or layout (use extract_code) or the full token list (use extract_design_tokens).

fresh.description: Skip the 24-hour cache and re-extract the live page - use when the site just changed and a cached result would be stale. Charged normally; the fresh result replaces the cached copy.

render.description: Run the page in a real browser first so its JavaScript executes - use for client-rendered (React/Next/SPA) sites, when a normal call came back thin, or after a 403 target_blocked (bot protection refuses plain HTTP requests but usually lets a browser through). Slower, and adds 5 credits to the call. Paid API plans and credit packs only: on a free account it returns 402 render_requires_plan and nothing runs - never pass it as a first attempt, and when a free account gets that error, retry without it and tell the user this page needs JS rendering, a paid feature. Free accounts still get rendering automatically when the SITE refuses the plain request (401/403/406): the server retries it in a browser at no charge, a few times a month, and the result carries usage.renderRescue explaining what happened - read that sentence out to the user when it appears.

screenshot.description: Requires render=true. Adds a screenshot field to the result: a public URL of a capture of the page (live 7 days), taken by the same browser that rendered it. Pass true for the 1440x900 viewport or 'full' for the entire page height. No extra credits beyond the render surcharge. Useful for showing the user what the extracted site looks like.

name: extract_brand

colorNames.description: Human-readable names for the role colors ("Royal Blue")

colors.description: Role colors as hex: primary, accent, background, text

confidence.description: 0-1: how much the site declared vs how much was inferred

logos.description: All icon/logo candidates, tagged by source

signals.description: WHY the result looks the way it does - the provenance behind `confidence`. Read `signals.explanation` and tell the user what it says instead of quoting the confidence number, which means nothing to them on its own. `primarySource` is the key field: 'css-var' or 'theme-color' means the site declared these colors and they are its real tokens; 'logo' means they were sampled from its logo; 'usage' means nothing was declared and the colors are a frequency-based GUESS - say so rather than presenting them as the brand's official palette.

declaredBackground.description: The background role came from a declared CSS variable

declaredLogo.description: A real logo was found, not just an og:image fallback

declaredText.description: The text role came from a declared CSS variable

explanation.description: One ready-to-relay sentence describing how much was declared vs inferred. Repeat this to the user when the extraction is uncertain.

fontsFound.description: How many font families resolved from the CSS cascade

primarySource.description: css-var | theme-color | logo | usage | null - where colors.primary came from, strongest first. 'usage' is inferred, not declared.

socials.description: Social profiles found on the page

truncation_note.description: Present when the result was trimmed - says what was dropped and how to get more.

typography.description: Fonts split by role: primary, mono

usage.description: Credit usage for the authed key (spent, remaining, monthly limit).
